samples.summary: Canonical design doc not updated for two new server-side refusals introduced by this module. `design-editor-engine.md` §5.7 states "**Two structural-op guards, both server-side** (`requireStatic`)" — scope must be `static`, and the node must be a direct JSX child. `jsx-nodes.mjs` ships a third structural guard (top-level returned element refused, jsx-nodes.mjs:766-773) and a new non-structural refusal for ambiguous component names (jsx-nodes.mjs:683-687, plus `findJsxRoots`'s `ambiguous` set, which §5.7's `SceneMeta.roots` paragraph does not mention). Both are behaviour of the published, contract-frozen API (`local-plugin.md` Risks: "jsx-nodes.mjs's child numbering … become compatibility surface the moment they hit npm"), so per CONTRIBUTING the canonical subsystem doc should record them rather than leaving the doc describing an earlier design.

The new top-level-return guard refuses a capability the spec grants. `resolveNode(..., {requireStatic:true})` refuses ANY node that is a member of `root.jsx`, i.e. the root element of every single-return component — which is the target of the most common structural op, "insert a child into the page's root <div>". The code's own comment (line 759) concedes this: "this refuses the node, so it also refuses inserting a CHILD into it, which is perfectly valid", and defers the correct op-aware guard to the inject.mjs PR. Engine §5.7 defines only the scope and direct-child guards, so this narrows the documented structural surface at the node model layer where the op is not knowable — arguably the wrong layer for the guard, and it silently removes the mainline insert-into-root case until a later PR widens `opts`.

`typescript` is a RUNTIME import of the module (`import ts from 'typescript'`, jsx-nodes.mjs:21) but is declared only under `devDependencies`. `design-editor-local-plugin.md` §2 makes dependency declaration the mechanical boundary test ("a reversal fails `pnpm install` in a consumer project rather than being caught in review"); the same discipline means the compiler this server half executes on must be a `dependency`/`peerDependency` of the published package, not a dev-only one. Harmless while `private: true`, but the packaging metadata is what §6 says has to become correct before publish.

`walkJsx(_sf, ...)` and `nodeAt(_sf, ...)` keep an unused first parameter justified as "a published API whose argument positions three consumers already call by" and "Dropping it would be a breaking change". No consumer exists in the tree — grep for `jsx-nodes` finds only this file, its test, the tsconfig and docs; `extract.mjs`/`inject.mjs`/`stamp.mjs` are not landed and the package is `private: true` and unpublished. The stated reason for the dead parameter is not true yet, so this is the cheapest moment to drop it rather than freeze it into the compatibility surface the local-plugin doc warns about.

`findJsxRoots` keeps a duplicated name in `roots` (last writer wins) while `resolveNode` permanently refuses that name. The doc comment calls `roots` "a complete index" so a future caller that can disambiguate is not locked out, but the immediate downstream consumer per `src/types.ts` is `SceneMeta.roots`, which the client renders as an outline — so an ambiguous helper will appear as an editable root whose every edit the server refuses, and the entry shown is whichever function was visited last. Either exclude ambiguous names from `roots` or record the intended split in the engine doc alongside the `SceneMeta.roots` paragraph.

The CP2 task item names the module's surface as "`walkJsx` / `fpOf` / `scopeOf` / `resolveNode`"; the landed file exposes no `scopeOf` (scope is carried on each walked entry instead). Likely a deliberate simplification, but the task list is the closest thing to the acceptance criteria here and still names an export that does not exist.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `design-editor-engine.md:754` states "**Two structural-op guards, both server-side** (`requireStatic`)" and lists exactly two bullets (scope must be `static`, 758-762; node must be a DIRECT JSX child, 763-766). The shipped module has a third refusal under `requireStatic` — the top-level returned element guard at jsx-nodes.mjs:765-773 (`isReturnsRoot(root) && root.jsx.includes(hit.node)`) — plus two further refusals the doc never mentions: the ambiguous-component-name refusal at jsx-nodes.mjs:678-687 (fed by `findJsxRoots`'s `ambiguous` set, which §5.7's `SceneMeta.roots` paragraph at 777-780 does not describe) and the synthetic-returns-root refusal at 719-724. I searched wider than the reviewer: grepped all of docs/ (not only docs/design/design-editor/) for `requireStatic` (one hit, line 754), `returns root|returned element|top-level return|returnsRoot|synthetic returns`, `ambiguous|ambiguity`, `sibling list|JSX-returning|whole return value|not editable`, `#returns|return statement|root.jsx|wrap it`, and `jsx-nodes|resolveNode|findJsxRoots`; also read design-editor-engine.md 690-825 and scanned design-editor-sandbox-recipe.md and design-editor-audit.md hits. No design doc anywhere records either refusal. The only non-code mentions are the unit tests (packages/design-editor/test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs) and task notes under docs/tasks/active/, neither of which is the canonical subsystem doc. Since `jsx-nodes.mjs` is explicitly marked stable/published API (design-editor-local-plugin.md:305, 338), these refusals are user-visible contract behaviour and the canonical doc is now factually wrong about the guard count — a design-doc-discipline (major) miss under this lens. No counterexample found, so the finding stays.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: jsx-nodes.mjs:765-773 adds a third `requireStatic` refusal that rejects any node identity-equal to a member of `root.jsx` — i.e. the root element of every single-return component — and its own comment at 759-764 concedes it therefore also refuses inserting a CHILD into that node ("which is perfectly valid"), deferring the op-aware guard to the later inject.mjs PR. The design doc grants only two guards: design-editor-engine.md:754-766 states "Two structural-op guards, both server-side (`requireStatic`)" and lists exactly scope-must-be-static and node-must-be-a-direct-JSX-child; the Phase-3 closeout repeats "the scope + direct-child guards enforced server-side" (line 1541-1543). Greps across docs/design for the third guard's rationale ("sibling list", "whole return value", "structural-op guard") find no documentation of a top-level-return refusal, so the implementation narrows the documented structural surface (notably the mainline `layout-insert` whose `parent` is the page root, per the intent table at line 257) without updating the canonical subsystem doc. That is a spec-conformance / design-doc-discipline mismatch in this lens's lane and major in kind. I considered refuting as unreachable since `requireStatic` currently has only test callers (test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:211-274) and no production caller, but that is an argument about timing rather than a guard making the code unreachable, and the refusal is deliberate published node-model behavior — not enough to drop the finding.
